title: A failed server-loader bulk_create_nodes answers 'nothing written' while its first 1,000 nodes stay committed
intended: docs/USER_GUIDE.md:238-241: with no caller transaction 'each write (... the bulk loaders ...) is a transaction of its own'; iris_vector_graph/_batch_check.py:68-80 (raise_if_missing: 'a writer raises it before its rollback, so nothing of the batch is written'); a GraphWriteError's text says what stayed written (4.7.0 row 14; the same rule F-0806 applies to Cypher).
observed: Trace 03/bulk (tr-replay-03): bulk_create_nodes of 2,000 nodes on a from_connect engine (two 1,000-node chunks to Graph.KG.EdgeScan.BulkIngestNodesSQL on the engine's own Native API process, iris_vector_graph/_engine/nodes_edges.py:1715-1757), the last node carrying a 70,000-character property value (wider than rdf_props.val VARCHAR(64000), schema.py:415; _check_create_nodes checks id, label and key widths only, nodes_edges.py:243-262). The journal shows the loader process commit chunk 1 (1,000 node rows) in its own transaction, chunk 2 rolled back (TROLLBACK 1 after SQLCODE -104 'property blob of tr03bk_1999'), and the SQL fallback on the cursor's process rolled back; the call raised GraphWriteError 'bulk_create_nodes failed, nothing written: IRIS refused 1 property row(s) of the batch ...' and a later SELECT counted 1,000 committed nodes. Replayed through wrt_bulk_atomic (as built) the trace ends in Raised with committed = (chunk 1, not chunk 2), violating WRT-B3.19; the reviewed design diverges at the first chunk's commit.
remedy: Run the loader chunks on the caller's process inside the WriteTxn (txn.native() in every case, the F-0305 fix), so a failed batch leaves nothing; until then, a failure after a committed chunk must say how many nodes stayed committed instead of 'nothing written'.
notes: Same mechanism as F-0305 (chunks committed by another process); F-0305's recorded observation is a successful call whose partial state another process could see mid-call. This is the failure path: the end state is partial and the reply states the opposite. Found by the trace-replay lane (AUDITE).
